category: Application Security, Injection Attacks & Web Exploits
code_snippet: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-2726c7f26c' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; require-trusted-types-for 'script';

content.tldr: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an HTTP header defense-in-depth standard that restricts which scripts, styles, and external origins the browser is permitted to load and execute.
content.simple_explanation: Even if an injection flaw permits an attacker to inject inline script markup into HTML, a robust CSP prevents browser execution by disallowing inline scripts by default (blocking unsafe-inline). Modern CSP architectures rely on cryptographically random, per-request nonces or cryptographic hashes. The browser only evaluates script tags carrying the exact matching nonce attribute, while disallowing unapproved external domains from exfiltrating data or loading secondary payloads.
content.real_world_example: A building security protocol: visitors can only speak to staff if they wear a tamper-evident badge carrying today's temporary stamp; even if a stranger enters uninvited, staff refuse to interact with anyone lacking the valid token.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Misconfigured CSPs that include 'unsafe-inline' or wildcard domain origins ('*') provide zero effective security against modern exploits. Always deploy CSP initially in 'Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only' mode to audit legitimate corporate scripts before enforcing blocks.
